title: Private deployments: pin Optimization Config version + operator rollback (installer/Helm/Terraform)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
Private customers (VPC/on-prem) need the same Optimization Config versioning model as Hosted/Dedicated, but with operator-controlled pinning and a low-risk rollback procedure that works without Redwood-managed control plane access.

This ticket delivers:
- A supported way to pin the active Optimization Config version for a Private deployment via (1) redwood-private-installer, (2) Helm values, and (3) Terraform.
- A supported rollback procedure that is safe under retries and avoids leaving the runtime in mixed version states.
- Clear operator UX and docs that match the new Console semantics (version IDs, scopes, rollback reason/audit trail), but do not require Console availability to execute rollback.

Goals / requirements
1) Pin active version (operator intent)
- Operator can set the active Optimization Config version for a given scope:
  - Minimum viable scope for Private GA: deployment-wide default (all tenants) + optional per-model override.
  - Stretch (post-GA): per-region scope (only if customer runs multi-region private control planes).
- Pin must be declarative and survive upgrades/restarts.

2) Rollback
- Operator can revert to a prior known-good Optimization Config version.
- Rollback is idempotent (safe to run twice).
- Rollback is fast and does not require editing multiple resources manually.
- Rollback must annotate the action for later forensics (who/when/what/why) in:
  - Audit logs (if audit logging configured), and
  - Kubernetes event / installer logs (always).

3) Sync semantics between components
- Control plane must reconcile the pinned version into the runtime apply pipeline.
- Workers must converge on the pinned version and expose current version for verification.
- No “split brain” between:
  - Helm/installer declared pin,
  - Control plane active pointer, and
  - Runtime worker-applied version.

4) Compatibility / constraints
- Must work in air-gapped environments.
- Must not require an external Redwood webhook/event stream.
- Must not expose secrets in values.yaml or logs.

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Full safe-apply canary automation in Private (we document manual gating and recommended checks).
- Multi-config transactional rollback across unrelated subsystems.

Implementation plan
A) Helm chart support (redwood-helm-charts)
- Add values:
  - optimizeConfig.activeVersion: string (e.g., "ocv_01J2...")
  - optimizeConfig.modelOverrides: string (YAML/JSON string blob for now; post-GA we can model as proper list)
- Render a ConfigMap consumed by the Private control plane (or a small sidecar) that informs the Optimization Config Service of the desired pinned version.
- Add chart docs:
  - How to pin
  - How to rollback (set version back + apply)
  - How to verify convergence

B) Installer support (redwood-private-installer)
- Add operator commands:
  - redwoodctl optimize-config status
  - redwoodctl optimize-config pin --version <id> [--model <name>] [--reason <text>]
  - redwoodctl optimize-config rollback --to-version <id> [--reason <text>]
- Command behavior:
  - Writes desired pin into the same declarative source of truth as Helm (values override file / rendered manifest patch).
  - Waits for reconciliation signal:
    - control plane reports active version == desired version
    - runtime workers report applied version == desired version
  - Emits a single summarized outcome line suitable for incident timelines.

C) Terraform support (redwood-terraform)
- Add resource/data source for Private pin:
  - redwood_optimization_config_pin (or equivalent)
- This should generate the same underlying k8s manifests/values needed by Helm.
- NOTE: keep scope limited to deployment-wide default in GA; model overrides in a follow-up if needed.

D) Verification hooks
- Ensure runtime response headers / metrics include config_version tag for Private (if feature enabled):
  - Metrics tag: config_version
  - Optional debug header: x-redwood-opt-config-version (behind a private-safe flag)
- Provide a kubectl-friendly check:
  - control plane endpoint /admin/optimize-config/active (auth-protected) OR
  - status reported in a ConfigMap updated by the reconciler.

E) Audit / security
- If audit logging is configured in Private, emit events for pin/rollback actions with:
  - actor (installer identity / k8s service account)
  - reason
  - from_version / to_version
  - request_id / correlation_id
- Ensure no sensitive prompt/eval data is included.
- Coordinate with Marcus Lin + Kevin Osei for field naming parity with Hosted audit events.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Operator can pin an Optimization Config version in Private via Helm values and observe control plane + workers converge.
- [x] Operator can rollback to a prior version via installer command in < 10 minutes (including convergence wait) under nominal cluster size.
- [x] Rollback command is idempotent and safe if interrupted and re-run.
- [x] Docs cover rollback prerequisites, verification steps, and common pitfalls.
- [x] Security review sign-off on audit/event payloads and logging behavior.

Test plan
- Unit: manifest rendering + installer argument parsing.
- Integration (kind/ephemeral cluster):
  - start with version A pinned → verify
  - change to version B pinned → verify
  - rollback to A → verify
  - interrupt rollback mid-way (kill installer) then re-run → verify convergence + no errors
- Failure injection:
  - control plane temporarily unavailable: installer should time out with actionable message and next steps.
  - partial worker pool restart during pin/rollback: reconcile should complete.

Operational notes
- Rollback should not flush KV cache unless required by runtime safety; if cache invalidation is needed, document expected transient latency increase and recommended off-peak timing.
- For Sev incidents: documented quick path is installer rollback command + verification checklist; Console may be unavailable in Private.

Follow-ups (post-GA)
- Structured modelOverrides field (avoid string blob).
- Optional per-region scoping for private multi-region.
- Optional “pause rollout” semantics when private customers choose to enable staged apply.
comments: 2025-11-22 (Vivek Kulkarni): Aligned with Ethan that Private GA scope will support deployment-wide default + per-model override only. Per-region deferred; most private customers run single region control plane per cluster.

2025-12-03 (Bruno Silva): Helm values approach confirmed. We’ll render desired pin into ConfigMap and have control plane reconcile into its active pointer. Avoid writing directly to DB to keep upgrades repeatable.

2025-12-11 (Marcus Lin): Security note: if we emit audit events in Private, actor identity must be explicit (service account + installer version), and reasons must be user-provided (or "unspecified"). No values.yaml logging of version if chart rendered with secrets alongside.
2026-01-08 (Vivek Kulkarni): Implemented installer commands in PR-19972. Waiting on runtime to expose applied version in health/status endpoint (dependency on ENG-4823).

2026-01-28 (Allison Grant): Metrics tagging in Private should match Hosted: tenant/model/region/config_version tags where available. For Private, tenant may be "_private_default" if single-tenant; document this.

2026-02-04 (Connor O'Brien): Release coordination: helm + installer + control plane must ship together for GA. Terraform can land slightly after but should not block Limited GA if docs mention Helm/installer path.

2026-02-12 (Vivek Kulkarni): Ran end-to-end drill on staging private cluster: pin A→B and rollback B→A successful. Second rollback attempt is no-op (idempotent) and returns success with "already at target" message.
2026-02-21 (Vivek Kulkarni): Marking Done. Docs updated and security sign-off received via Marcus/Kevin review. Tracking structured modelOverrides and per-region scoping as follow-up tickets.
